summary:
Round 2, TEST review, re-measured on the staged bytes. Both round-1 minors are closed by measurement rather than by argument.
(1) THE SURVIVOR IS DEAD. `return key.equals(keyFor(sequence));` -> `return true;` now fails LogKeysTest:52, and it is the ONLY failure in the 253-test sequencer suite -- which independently re-confirms the round-1 finding that the end-to-end file cannot reach that half.
(2) `CommitLog.isEntryKey` is gone; `grep -rn isEntryKey --include=*.java .` finds only the LogKeys definition, LogKeysTest and the two ChainReplay call sites, and `git show HEAD:...CommitLog.java` never had it, so the deletion removes surface this commit invented.
EACH NEW TEST KILLS SOMETHING NO OTHER TEST DOES, measured one mutation at a time, whole suite each time: test 1 is the sole killer of `Long.parseUnsignedLong` -> `Integer.parseUnsignedInt` (only the Long.MAX_VALUE assertion reaches it; every other test in the repo uses small sequences). Test 2 is the sole killer of three DIFFERENT mutants at three DIFFERENT lines: `return true` at :52 (unpadded), `equals` -> `equalsIgnoreCase` at :56 (uppercase), and `key.equals(keyFor(s))` -> `key.endsWith(keyFor(s).substring(logPrefix.length()))` at :60 (seventeen digits -- the only case where the canonical tail is a suffix of the candidate). Test 3 kills the bare-`endsWith` predicate, jointly with test 2 and ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest.
NO CASE IS MISFILED. All four keys in test 2 were checked against the real JDK to actually PARSE -- "9"->9, "000000000000000A"->10, "00000000000000009"->9, "+000000000000009"->9 -- so all four genuinely reach the canonicalisation they claim to pin; the leading-plus and seventeen-digit comments are accurate. The leading-plus case is the one assertion for which I could construct no mutation it uniquely kills; it is not vacuous (it reaches the round trip and is refused only there) and it documents a real JDK edge, so it stays -- recorded only so the file is not credited with four independent kills when it has three.
TEST 1'S SELF-REFERENCE IS ANCHORED. `isEntryKey(keyFor(n))` would survive a joint mutation of both halves, but the writer side is pinned by literal keys elsewhere: `%016x` -> `%x` in `LogKeys.keyFor` fails LogKeysTest:52, CommitLogTest.theKeyCarriesTheEpochZeroPadded... and LocalSequencerFailoverTest, which also proves the new `CommitLog` delegates are exercised by the existing suite.
BOTH LISTING SITES ARE PINNED SEPARATELY. Exactly two `store.list(` call sites exist in sequencer/src/main; neutering only chainEnd's filter fails 2 tests, only applyChain's fails 3, and neither site is carried by the other's tests. ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest is unchanged since round 1 and was not re-reviewed in depth, per instruction.
RULES 4-5: no existing test file appears in the diff at all (two new test files, one new main file, a delegation change, a javadoc edit, a method deletion), so no assertion can have been weakened; check-test-integrity.sh and check-tdd.sh both green (7 new tests, all observed failing first).
TIER: T0, no store/socket/clock/sleep/port/system-temp. The `LogKeys` split is what makes T0 reachable without constructing a writer.
ROW CLAIMS SPOT-CHECKED: `return false` fails 32 tests -- measured 32 exactly; 741 tests green -- measured 741 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors after `./gradlew test --rerun-tasks`, a cached green not accepted as evidence. Tree restored byte-identical: `git diff` empty, staged set unchanged.

findings.title: Two mutations survive the whole suite: deleting either half of the guard in isEntryKey. Equivalent today, but one of them stops being equivalent the moment a caller passes a key it did not get from list().
findings.surviving_mutation: `if (!key.startsWith(logPrefix) || !key.endsWith(SUFFIX))` -> `if (!key.endsWith(SUFFIX))`, and separately -> `if (!key.startsWith(logPrefix))`. Both leave `./gradlew :sequencer:test` GREEN (exit 0, 253 tests). Measured, not argued.
findings.failure_scenario: Both are equivalent under today's callers, because `keyFor` always emits logPrefix + 16 hex + ".delta" and so `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))` already forces both properties -- that is why no test catches them and why they should be argued rather than killed. The startsWith one is NOT equivalent in general: without it, a key that ends in ".delta" but is shorter than logPrefix.length() + 6 makes `key.substring(begin > end)` throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false. Unreachable from both current call sites, which only pass keys from `store.list(logPrefix, ...)`. It becomes reachable the moment M4.8b2's checkpoint writer -- or anything else -- asks `isEntryKey` about a key it did not obtain from that LIST, and recovery would then die on an unchecked exception rather than skipping the key. No test constrains that, and the javadoc does not state the precondition. Not blocking under review.md: nothing in the staged behaviour is wrong, and no acceptance criterion is unpinned. If check-mutants.sh lands, these two belong in baselines/mutants.txt as argued-equivalent, not as kills.

measurements: return key.equals(keyFor(sequence)) -> return true  => LogKeysTest:52 only (was: whole suite green in round 1)
isEntryKey -> return key.endsWith(SUFFIX)           => LogKeysTest x2 + ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest
restored tree: ./gradlew test --rerun-tasks => 741 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors; git diff empty
